title: Tuna Salad Sandwich
notes: 2 servings, 1 to 2 sandwiches. Prep 10 min, total 10 min. If using tuna packed in water, drain it and add 1 tablespoon of good extra virgin olive oil. If using tuna packed in olive oil, use it undrained, or drain and add back 2 teaspoons of your own oil. Cottage cheese is the unusual addition and the point of the recipe - it adds creaminess and protein. Doubles easily; leftovers keep 3 to 4 days refrigerated.
ingredients: 1 (5- or 6-ounce) can tuna packed in olive oil, undrained
A pinch or two fresh dill, chopped
steps: Combine the ingredients: in a medium bowl, toss together the canned tuna, cottage cheese, mayonnaise, red onion, celery, capers, lemon juice, dill, parsley and Dijon mustard until combined.
Make the sandwich: serve the tuna salad on toast, either open faced or between two slices of bread with lettuce and tomatoes, if you wish. For a low-carb option, serve on sliced lettuce.

title: Avocado Tuna Salad
notes: Serves 4. Prep 15 min, total 16 min. Water-packed tuna keeps the fat content controllable; choose firm but ripe avocados so they don't go mushy when tossed.
ingredients: 1 cup English cucumber, quartered and sliced
steps: Place the tuna, cucumber, avocado, red onion and cilantro in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together the lime juice, olive oil, chili powder, cumin and salt and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the tuna mixture; gently toss to coat. Serve immediately.

title: Egg Salad
notes: Makes 1 serving. Total 15 min. Tastes great warm but can be eaten cold. NOTE: the link in the original list was labelled 'Egg Salad' but points at this Swiss chard farro salad.
ingredients: 3 Swiss chard leaves, stems removed, thinly sliced
steps: Fill a large skillet or saucepan with 3 inches of water and bring to a boil. Add salt.
Fill a bowl with iced water. Blanch Swiss chard leaves one at a time: submerge in boiling water 15 seconds, until bright green. Transfer to ice water for 1 minute. Dry thoroughly with paper towels.
In another bowl, whisk vinegar, oil, cumin, and salt and pepper. Add chard, farro, and grapes. Toss to coat.
Serve warm, topped with shaved Parmesan and egg.

title: Farro Bowl
notes: Prep 20 min, cook 30 min, total 50 min. Vegan as written. Good for meal prep; keeps 3 days.
ingredients: 1 medium head of broccoli, cut into bite-sized florets
Fine sea salt and freshly-cracked black pepper
1 batch dreamy tahini dressing (tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt, pepper)
Half of a medium red onion, thinly sliced
1/3 cup sliced or slivered almonds, toasted
steps: Roast the broccoli. Heat oven to 450F. Spread the florets on a misted baking sheet, drizzle with olive oil and toss to coat. Season with salt and pepper. Roast 15-20 minutes, until slightly charred and crispy at the edges.
Cook the farro in a medium saucepan in the vegetable stock instead of water, per package directions. Once al dente, drain off any extra stock.
Prepare the dressing. Whisk all ingredients together until combined.
In a large bowl, combine the cooked farro, roasted broccoli, arugula, chickpeas, red onion, and half of the almonds. Drizzle with the dressing and toss.
Serve warm, garnished with the remaining almonds, or refrigerate up to 3 days.

title: Farro Salad
notes: Serves 4. Prep 15 min, cook 5 min. Assumes the farro is already cooked. Bulgur, couscous, brown rice or quinoa all substitute.
steps: To make the dressing, combine the tahini, water, lemon juice, minced garlic, cumin, cayenne, and salt in a blender. Blend until smooth. Refrigerate until ready to use, up to 5 days.

Rinse and drain the chickpeas. Heat the olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium. Add the chickpeas and sprinkle over the smoked paprika, garlic powder, cayenne if using, and cracked pepper. Stir to coat, then saute about 5 minutes until slightly browned and blistered. Salt to taste.
Chop the tomatoes, cucumber, and parsley. Place about 3/4 cup cooked farro in each bowl, then top with tomato, cucumber, spiced chickpeas, and a pinch of parsley. Drizzle the dressing over and serve.

title: Mediterranean Couscous Salad
notes: Serves 6. Prep 20 min, cook 10 min. Many readers double the dressing to serve extra on the side.
ingredients: 1/2 cup kalamata olives, pitted and sliced
steps: Cook the couscous. In a medium saucepan bring the water, salt, and olive oil to a boil over high heat. Add the couscous and stir quickly. Turn off the heat, cover, and let stand 5 minutes until tender. Fluff with a fork and let cool, refrigerating to speed it up.
Assemble. In a large bowl combine the cooled couscous, tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, garbanzo beans, red onion, olives, feta, parsley, mint, basil, and oregano.
Make the lemon dressing. Whisk together the lemon zest, lemon juice, vinegar, salt, and pepper, then slowly drizzle in the olive oil, whisking until thickened.
Pour the dressing over the salad and stir gently to combine. Garnish with more feta and fresh herbs.

title: Overnight Oats
notes: Serves 1. Prep 5 min. Amounts were not captured from the page - check the source for measurements. Scales by doubling/tripling in one bowl. Use a 16oz jar if adding toppings. Toppings: fresh or dried fruit, nuts and seeds, nut butter, cinnamon, protein powder.
steps: In a small jar, stir together the oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds, and maple syrup.
Place the jar in the fridge and let the oats soak at least two hours, though overnight is best.
The next morning, add your favorite toppings and enjoy, or scoop into a bowl and top from there.

title: Salmon Avocado Salad
notes: Yield 2 to 4. Total 30 min. Any orange works; grapefruit is divisive, so test it first. Dressing keeps a week in the fridge.
ingredients: 12 ounces spring greens, baby spinach or romaine
steps: Preheat the broiler to high and set the oven rack about 6 inches below it.
Place the salmon on a baking sheet and brush with the grapeseed oil. Season with the salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Broil the salmon 6 to 8 minutes, until just opaque and flaking easily. A large filet takes 8 to 10 minutes; time depends on thickness.
For the vinaigrette, whisk together the vinegar, lemon juice, honey, garlic, salt and pepper, then whisk continuously while streaming in the olive oil.
Toss the lettuce with a pinch of salt and pepper, the orange segments, grapefruit, avocado and shallot. Drizzle with the vinaigrette and sprinkle with feta before serving.

title: Salmon Avocado Salad 2
notes: Serves 2. Prep 10 min, cook 10 min. Leftover dressing works on future salads or as a chicken marinade.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Season the salmon filets with salt and pepper. Add the filets top side down and cook 4-5 minutes.
Flip the salmon and cook another 2-3 minutes, until mostly opaque with just a smidge of softness in the middle.
Divide the other salad ingredients between two bowls, then place the cooked salmon on top.
Mix the dressing ingredients in a small bowl and drizzle over.

title: Salmon Bowl
notes: 6 servings. 40 min. Parve, low carb, pescatarian. Contains soy and gluten. For dinner rather than lunch, increase the salmon to six ounces per person.
ingredients: 3 cups cooked brown rice or quinoa
steps: Preheat oven to 400F. Squeeze lemon or lime juice onto the salmon fillets, then season with salt and pepper. Cook 12 minutes or until flaky.
Spray a nonstick frying pan with cooking spray and saute the garlic until fragrant. Add the spinach, season well with salt and pepper, and cook until wilted.
Place rice in the bottom of each bowl, then add salmon, broccoli, avocado, garlic spinach, and baby corn.
Use a julienne peeler or sharp knife to cut thin strips of cucumber and carrot and add to the bowls.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, honey, and ginger and drizzle over the bowls, then top with sesame seeds.

title: Blacked Fish
notes: Serves 4. Total 15 min. Blackened means coated in Cajun spice, not burnt. Sole or another white fish substitutes; watch closely so it does not overcook.
ingredients: 1 lime, cut into wedges (optional, for serving)
steps: Combine the paprika, brown sugar, oregano, garlic powder, cumin, cayenne and salt in a small bowl, using your fingers to break up lumps of brown sugar. Sprinkle the rub evenly over both sides of the tilapia fillets.
Heat the olive oil over medium-high heat in a large non-stick pan. Cook the fillets 2 to 3 minutes per side, until reddish-brown outside and flaky inside. Serve immediately with lime wedges.

title: Lemon Mint Barley Salad
notes: Serves 4. Ready in 40 min. Adapted from Cooking Light. Good at room temperature, so it travels well for lunch. The lemon zest goes in with the dressing.
steps: Combine 1/4 teaspoon salt and the water in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil. Stir in the barley, cover, reduce heat, and simmer 30 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat, cover and let stand 5 minutes.
Spoon the barley into a large bowl and cool slightly. Add the mint, tomato, green onions, capers, and olives and stir well.
Whisk the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, red pepper and oil together, drizzle over the barley mixture, and toss gently to coat.

title: Chickpea Salad Sandwich
notes: Serves 4. Prep 15 min. Vegan with vegan mayo; gluten-free in lettuce wraps or on GF bread. Keeps about 4 days refrigerated, so it is a good make-ahead lunch. Adapted from The Oh She Glows Cookbook.
ingredients: 15 oz canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1/4 cup finely chopped red bell pepper
1/8 tsp dried dill, or fresh to taste
2 TBSP fresh chopped basil, plus extra to taste
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas and add them to a large bowl. Mash with a potato masher until the texture appears flaked, almost like tuna salad, following up with a fork. A food processor also works.
Chop the green onion, celery, shredded carrots, pepper, and pickles.
Add to the bowl with the chickpeas, then add the mayo, dijon, yellow mustard, dill, salt, and pepper. Stir well to coat.
Fold in the sunflower seeds and basil and adjust to taste.
Pile high on bread with your sandwich fixings, or enjoy as a wrap, with crackers, or on a salad.

title: Quinoa Fried Rice
notes: Makes 4 servings. Prep 5 min, cook 10 min. Chilling the cooked quinoa first is essential - spread it on a baking sheet and refrigerate 15 minutes. Cooking the quinoa in veggie stock adds flavour.
ingredients: 3-4 tablespoons soy sauce, or more to taste
steps: Heat 1/2 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium-high until melted. Add the egg and cook until scrambled, stirring occasionally. Remove to a separate plate.

Add another 1 tablespoon butter to the pan and heat until melted. Add the carrots, onion, peas and garlic and season with a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Saute about 5 minutes until the onion and carrots are soft.

Increase heat to high, add the remaining 1 1/2 tablespoons butter and stir until melted. Immediately add the cooked quinoa, green onions, soy sauce and oyster sauce if using, and stir until combined. Keep stirring another 3 minutes to fry the quinoa.
Add the eggs and stir to combine, then add the sesame oil, stir, and remove from heat. Serve warm.

title: Stir Fry
notes:
protein pasta, double chickpeas and blackbeans
4 servings. Prep 15 min, cook 15 min. Most amounts were not captured from the page - check the source for measurements. Keeps 3-4 days refrigerated. Tofu, chicken, shrimp or a fried egg all work as add-ins.
ingredients: 1/3 cup low sodium soy sauce or coconut aminos
Stir fry rice noodles (or ramen or soba)
steps: Whisk together all of the sauce ingredients in a bowl until well combined and set aside.
Cook the veggies down in a little sesame oil in a pot until tender but still with a bite.
While the veggies cook, cook the stir fry noodles according to the package directions.
Stir the drained chickpeas into the pot with the veggies. Turn the heat to low and add the stir fry sauce.
Once the sauce has thickened a bit, stir in the cooked noodles, basil, and cashews.

title: Copycat Panera Strawberry Poppyseed Salad
notes: Makes 2 servings. Amounts were not captured from the page - check the source for measurements. Panera's version has grilled chicken; this one is vegetarian. Prep components ahead and dress right before serving; leftovers keep 3 days undressed.
ingredients: Romaine lettuce (or spinach or baby kale)
steps: Prep the ingredients: chop the lettuce, strawberries, and pineapple.
Plate the lettuce and top with the fruit and pecans.
Whisk together the homemade Greek yogurt poppyseed dressing.
Drizzle with the poppyseed dressing and serve immediately.

title: Easy Chicken Quesadillas
notes: Serves 6. Prep 10 minutes, cook 20 minutes, total 30 minutes.
ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, cut into small pieces
1/2 large bell pepper, diced, any color
steps: Preheat a skillet with oil on medium heat. Add in the chicken and taco seasoning. Cook for 4 minutes.
Add in the bell pepper and onion, cook for another 5 minutes or until chicken and veggies gain color and are cooked through. Set aside.
On a clean skillet, add a bit of butter or oil and place a tortilla on top. Add Mexican cheese and chicken mixture to one half of the tortilla. Top with more cheese. Fold the tortilla over to close.

Cook for a few minutes and once the tortilla is golden on one side, flip and cook for a few more minutes until the second side is golden brown. Make sure that the cheese has melted. Repeat with the rest of the quesadillas.
Serve while the quesadillas are still warm.

title: Fall Veggies Rice Harvest Bowls
notes: Serves 4. Prep 10 minutes, cook 30 minutes, total 40 minutes. The chicken is optional - cooked steak, roasted chickpeas, or baked salmon all work. Pre-cut veggies save time. To meal prep, store the dressing separately and assemble just before eating; bowls keep 4 days refrigerated without the dressing. Wild rice can be made ahead or in an Instant Pot (rinse 1 1/2 cups wild rice blend, add 1 1/2 cups water, cook on high pressure 15 minutes, quick release, fluff).
ingredients: 2 cups diced sweet potatoes (about 2 large sweet potatoes)
2 cups cubed red onion (about 1 medium onion)
2-3 Tablespoons water (as needed to thin to drizzle consistency)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
Place the vegetables on a baking sheet and drizzle with the avocado oil.
Sprinkle all the seasonings over the veggies and toss them to coat them in oil and spices.
Roast the vegetables for about 30 minutes, tossing halfway to ensure that they are evenly cooked. The vegetables should be tender.
While the vegetables are roasting, combine the dressing ingredients except the water in a small bowl.
Whisk until smooth and add water a little at a time to reach a drizzle consistency.
Add 3/4 cup cooked rice to 4 bowls along with 1/4 cup chopped spinach.
Divide the roasted veggies between the bowls, then top with pepitas and dressing.
Serve and enjoy.

title: 20 Minute Korean Gochujang Beef Bowls
notes: Serves 6. Prep 10 minutes, cook 10 minutes, total 20 minutes. For a milder version use only 1 tablespoon gochujang. Cauliflower rice works in place of rice. Best served straight off the stove, but it reheats well.
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds ground beef (or chicken or pork)
1/4 cup pickled ginger (or 1 tablespoon fresh grated ginger)
2 tablespoons ginger juice or rice vinegar
steps: In a large skillet, combine the beef and a pinch of black pepper. Cook over medium heat, breaking up the meat as it cooks until browned, about 5 minutes. Add the butter, peppers, garlic, shallots, and ginger. Cook 2 minutes.

Pour over the tamari, add the Gochujang, ginger juice, and 1/3 cup water. Cook until the sauce coats the beef, 2-3 minutes. Mix in the maple/honey and cook another 1-2 minutes until the beef is caramelized. Remove from the heat. Toss with sesame seeds.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, mix the cucumbers with 1 teaspoon salt, the chile flakes, ginger juice, and green onions. Let sit 5 minutes.
Serve the beef and peppers over bowls of rice. Serve with the cucumber salad and top with peanuts. Add spicy mayo if desired.

title: Greek Chicken Bowls with Tahini Feta Sauce
notes: Serves 6. Prep 25 minutes, cook 20 minutes, total 45 minutes. Spicy Greek seasoning: mix 2 teaspoons dried oregano, 1 teaspoon dried rosemary, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon onion powder, and 1/2 teaspoon chipotle chili powder. Harissa oil: combine 1 tablespoon red harissa sauce, 3 tablespoons toasted sesame oil, 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika, and 1/2 teaspoon chili powder, then season with salt. Quinoa works in place of rice, and thighs stay juicier than breasts. For make-ahead lunches, pack grains, kale, and chicken separately and keep the sauce in a jar.
ingredients: chili flakes, salt, and black pepper
1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts or thighs, cubed
3 tablespoons sesame seeds or pine nuts
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F.

On a baking sheet, toss the chicken with 2 tablespoons olive oil, the Dijon, garlic, Greek/Italian seasoning, honey, chili flakes, salt, and pepper. Bake 15 minutes, toss and bake another 5-10 minutes, or until cooked through.

Meanwhile, combine the kale, 2 tablespoons olive oil, lemon juice, olives, pepperoncini, sesame seeds, salt, and chili flakes. If desired, add the kale to the sheet pan with chicken during the last 1-2 minutes of cooking to wilt the kale.
To make the feta sauce, combine all ingredients and 1/4 cup water in a blender and blend until smooth. If needed, add water to thin the sauce as desired. Season to taste with salt and chili flakes.
Serve the kale salad and chicken over bowls of rice. Drizzle over the feta sauce and spicy oil. Top with dill.

title: Avocado Breakfast Bowl
notes: Serves 2. Prep 5 minutes, cook 20 minutes, total 25 minutes.
ingredients: 1 pinch salt and ground black pepper to taste
steps: Stir water and quinoa together in a rice cooker; cook until quinoa is tender, about 15 minutes.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook eggs to desired doneness; season with seasoned salt and pepper.
Combine quinoa and eggs in a bowl; top with avocado and feta cheese.

title: Cheesy Asparagus
notes: Serves 4. Prep 5 minutes, cook 15 minutes, total 20 minutes. Cheddar, gruyere, provolone, or Swiss can stand in for the mozzarella and Parmesan. Keep the spears in a single layer so they roast rather than steam, and adjust timing for very thin or very thick spears. For crispier cheese, broil for a minute or two at the end. A squeeze of fresh lemon before serving brightens the flavor.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (204 degrees C).
In a medium baking dish, toss the asparagus with olive oil, minced garlic, Italian seasoning, sea salt, and black pepper.
Bake asparagus for 7-9 minutes, until the asparagus is bright green and just starting to soften, but not fully done.
Mix together the mozzarella and Parmesan cheeses, then sprinkle over the asparagus.
Return to the oven for another 6-8 minutes, until the cheese is melted and golden.

title: Keto caramelized endives
notes: Serves 4. For a lunch, top an arugula salad with the caramelized endive and pair with a couple of eggs.
steps: Cut the endives into inch-sized pieces.
Melt butter in a large frying pan over high heat and add endive to the frying pan.
Stir and continue to fry on lower heat until the endive is soft and browned.
Be sure that most of the liquid evaporates so that the endive will be caramelized properly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve with finely chopped chives or parsley. Enjoy as a side dish or gourmet topping on salads.

title: Keto Roasted Vegetables
notes: Serves 8 (about 1 cup each). Prep 10 minutes, cook 25 minutes, total 35 minutes. Works with any vegetables as long as you pair ones with similar roasting times, or cut the slower-cooking ones smaller. Optional additions: 2 tablespoons balsamic drizzled partway through, or 1/3 cup parmesan tossed in with the oil and seasonings. Keeps 3-4 days refrigerated; reheat in an air fryer or a 350 degree F oven.
ingredients: 2 cups broccoli (1 crown cut into florets, about 2 inches long with 1.5-inch heads)
2 cups cauliflower (cut into 2-inch-long florets; about 1/2 head)
2 cups zucchini (sliced into thick circles, 3/8-inch thick; about 8 ounces)
2 cups bell peppers (cut into 1.5 inch pieces; about 1.5 large peppers)
2 cups red onion (cut into 1.5 inch pieces; about 1 medium onion)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (218 degrees C). Line an extra-large baking sheet with foil or you can leave it bare. Spray with cooking spray.
Combine all the vegetables in a large bowl. Drizzle with olive oil, and season with garlic powder, Italian seasoning, sea salt, and black pepper. Toss to coat.
Arrange the vegetables in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, making sure each piece is touching the pan. Do not crowd the pan - use multiple pans if needed.
Roast the vegetables in the oven for 15 minutes, on the rack one higher than the middle rack.
Use tongs or a large turner to toss or flip the pieces. Roast for 8-15 more minutes, until the veggies are tender. If you want them browned, place them under the broiler for 2-3 minutes.

title: Roasted Parsnips
notes: Yields about 4 cups; total time 35 minutes. Amounts were not captured from the page - check the source for measurements. Pick parsnips about 1 inch thick at the top and of even size; smaller ones burn more easily. You do not need to core them unless they are overgrown and woody. Parsnips can be cut up to four days ahead and stored in the fridge; toss with oil and seasonings just before roasting. Leftovers keep three days refrigerated. Variations: finish with balsamic or lemon, add grated Parmesan after roasting, or drizzle with honey butter in the last few minutes.
ingredients: Parsnips, peeled and cut into 1-inch oblique chunks
Dried Greek seasoning blend (or Italian seasoning or Herbes de Provence)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F - slightly cooler than most roasted vegetables, since parsnips are high in sugar and burn easily.
Peel the parsnips to remove the bitter, tough outer skin, then cut them into bias-cut chunks about 1 inch each, rolling them a half turn between cuts if desired.
Toss with olive oil, salt, and the dried seasoning blend.
Spread out on a baking sheet in a single layer and roast, stirring once or twice since the bottoms brown first.
Roast 25 to 35 minutes depending on the size of the chunks, until a fork slides in with little resistance.

title: Mediterranean Zucchini Noodle Pasta
notes: Also good served cold as a salad. Add chicken or shrimp to make it a one-pot meal.
ingredients: sea salt and black pepper, to taste
2 tbsp Italian flat leaf parsley, chopped
steps: In a large saute pan, over medium heat, add zucchini, spinach, olive oil, butter, garlic, sea salt and black pepper. Saute until zucchini is tender and spinach is wilted. Drain excess liquid.
To the pan, add sun-dried tomatoes, capers, parsley, and kalamata olives. Mix in and saute 2-3 minutes.
Remove from heat and toss with Parmesan and feta cheeses before serving.

title: Butternut Squash Noodles
notes: Serves 4. Prep 10 minutes, cook 15 minutes, total 25 minutes. Start with a small amount of salt and add more after the parmesan only if needed. Spiralize the long neck of the squash, not the seeded bulb. Alternatives to sauteing: boil like spaghetti for 3-5 minutes, or roast at 400 F for 7-9 minutes. Swap fresh sage for the parsley for a holiday version, and omit the parmesan (or use nutritional yeast) to make it vegan. Leftovers keep about a day; raw spiralized squash freezes up to a month.
ingredients: 6 cups spiralized butternut squash noodles, from two 10-12 inch butternut squashes
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add in the onion and cook until translucent, 3-4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and cook, stirring constantly, for 30 seconds.

Add in the butternut squash noodles and cook for 7-10 minutes (timing depends on the thickness of your noodles). Use kitchen tongs to gently turn them as they cook. They are done when they soften and get smaller in volume.
Add in the walnuts and give it a large gentle stir.
Divide the cooked noodles into bowls and sprinkle each bowl with parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley, if preferred.

title: Grilled Boy Choy
notes: Serves 4. Prep 5 minutes, cook 10 minutes, total 15 minutes.
steps: Preheat a grill to medium.
Halve the bok choy lengthwise; microwave, covered, 3 to 5 minutes.
Whisk the sweet chili sauce with the rice vinegar, brown sugar, sesame oil and soy sauce. Toss with the bok choy.
Grill until charred, 1 to 2 minutes per side, brushing with any extra sauce.

title: Caprese Zoodles
notes: Serves 4.
ingredients: 1 cup mozzarella balls, quartered if large
steps: Using a spiralizer, create zoodles out of zucchini.
Add zoodles to a large bowl, toss with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Let marinate 15 minutes.
Add tomatoes, mozzarella and basil to zoodles and toss until combined.
Drizzle with balsamic and serve.

title: Garlic Green Beans
notes: Serves 4. Inspired by Sichuan dry-fried string beans. Resist stirring the beans constantly - let them take on color, patience is essential here.
ingredients: 1 lb. green beans, trimmed, patted dry of any surface moisture or condensation
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet over high until shimmering. Add green beans (the dryer they are, the less they will spatter when they hit the oil) and cook, covering skillet as needed if beans are spattering, until browned underneath, about 3 minutes. Turn beans with tongs and redistribute so they brown evenly. Continue to cook, turning occasionally, until browned all over and tender, about 5 minutes longer. Season with salt. Add garlic, capers, and red pepper flakes. Cook, tossing occasionally, just until garlic turns golden, about 1 minute.
Transfer beans to a platter. Spoon caper-garlic mixture over and pour some oil over too; season with salt.

title: Jalepeno Corn
notes: Serves 8. Prep 15 minutes, cook 4 hours. You can substitute 2 pounds fresh corn kernels or drained canned whole-kernel corn for the frozen corn. Stovetop version: simmer the ingredients in a heavy saucepan or Dutch oven over low heat until creamy and tender. Oven version: bake in a casserole dish at 350 F for 30 to 40 minutes. Wear gloves when cutting the peppers. Keeps three days refrigerated or three months frozen.
ingredients: 1 package (8 ounces) cream cheese, softened and cubed
4 jalapeno peppers, seeded and finely chopped
steps: In a 3-quart slow cooker, combine all ingredients.
Cover and cook on low for 4-5 hours or until corn is tender, stirring occasionally.

title: Garlic Broccoli
notes: Serves 4. Active time 15 minutes, total time 35 minutes. The garlic is sliced rather than minced so it is less prone to burning and stays mellower.
ingredients: 2 heads of broccoli (1 1/4 pounds total), stems peeled and heads halved lengthwise
1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, plus more to taste
steps: In a large, deep skillet, heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil. Add the broccoli, cut side down, cover, and cook over moderate heat until richly browned on the bottom, about 8 minutes.
Add the water, cover, and cook until the broccoli is just tender and the water has evaporated, about 7 minutes.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil along with the garlic and the crushed red pepper; cook uncovered until the garlic is golden brown, about 3 minutes. Drizzle with the lemon juice, season the broccoli with salt and black pepper, and serve.

title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts & Cauliflower
notes: Yields 12 servings. Prep 25 minutes, cook 20-25 minutes. Golden cauliflower works well in place of white.
steps: In a large skillet, cook bacon over medium heat until crisp, stirring occasionally. Remove with a slotted spoon; drain on paper towels. Discard drippings, reserving 1 tablespoon.
In a large bowl, mix the garlic, oil, butter, salt, pepper and reserved drippings. Add Brussels sprouts and cauliflower; toss to coat. Transfer to 2 greased 15x10x1-in. baking pans.
Bake at 400° for 20-25 minutes. Sprinkle each pan with 2 tablespoons cheese. Bake 5 minutes longer or until vegetables are tender. Sprinkle with bacon and, if desired, additional cheese.

title: Fall Veggie Blend
notes: Serves 6; plan on a heaping cup per person. Prep 20 minutes, cook 30 minutes. Sumac is a Middle Eastern spice with a citrusy flavor — lemon zest or lemon pepper can substitute. Leftovers can be pulverized in a food processor and stirred into pasta sauce.
ingredients: 6 medium-large carrots, peeled and halved vertically
1 cup small Brussels sprouts, stems trimmed and halved vertically
2 cups butternut squash, peeled and cut into bite size cubes
1 1/2 cups red onion, peeled and sliced into wedges or bite-size pieces
2 medium golden beets (about 1 cup), peeled and cut into 1/2 inch slices vertically
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.

In a large bowl combine the olive oil, balsamic vinegar and sumac. Add the prepared vegetables and toss to fully coat with the liquid. Rub any remaining liquid into the vegetables by hand (be careful of the beets as they can stain clothing), especially the carrots which are more difficult to coat when in longer form.

Place vegetables on a large baking sheet or roasting pan and sprinkle the salt over them. Flip the vegetables halfway through cooking. Cook until done but still firm (not mushy), about 30 minutes. Serve immediately.

title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts
notes: Yields 3 servings. Prep 5 minutes, total 20 minutes. Endlessly riffable — chili flakes, cumin seeds, or fresh oregano all work, and shaved Parmesan makes a good garnish.
steps: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat oil. Once hot, add your Brussels sprouts and shake pan so all cut sides of sprouts settle cut side down in a single layer. Cook undisturbed 5 to 7 minutes, until cut sides of sprouts become caramelized.
Stir and continue to cook until sprouts have taken on color and become tender, 6 to 8 minutes more. Season with salt and pepper, squeeze lemon, and add garlic. Stir and cook 1 minute longer.

title: Summer Vegetables
notes: Serves 4. Prep 10 minutes, cook 40 minutes. Any mix of vegetables works — just don't overcrowd the baking sheet or they steam instead of roasting. Don't skimp on the oil, and add a final pinch of salt after roasting.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400ºF. Wash and chop the vegetables into approximately 1-inch pieces.

Spread the vegetables out over a large baking sheet (or two, if needed) so they're in a single layer and not piled on top of one another. Drizzle the olive oil over top, then add the basil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Toss the vegetables until they're evenly coated in oil and spices.

Roast the vegetables for 30-40 minutes, stirring once or twice (every 15-20 minutes or so), until the vegetables are soft and browned on the edges. Taste the vegetables and add another pinch of salt if desired. Sprinkle fresh chopped parsley over top just before serving.

title: Cheesy Broccoli
notes: Serves 6. Prep 10 minutes, cook 25 minutes. This makes very crispy garlic; if you're worried it will burn or turn bitter, add it in the last 5-7 minutes of cooking coated in a little oil. Dry the broccoli thoroughly after washing — the drier it is, the more it crisps.
ingredients: Good olive oil (or, for keto, butter flavor coconut oil)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F/200°C.

Cut the broccoli florets from the thick stalks, leaving an inch or two of stalk attached to the florets, discarding the rest of the stalks. Cut the larger pieces through the base of the head with a small knife, pulling the florets apart. You should have about 8 cups of florets.
Place the broccoli florets on a sheet pan large enough to hold them in a single layer. Toss the garlic on the broccoli and drizzle with 5 tablespoons olive oil. Sprinkle with the salt and pepper.
Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, until crisp-tender and the tips of some of the florets are browned.
Remove the broccoli from the oven and immediately toss with 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, the lemon zest, lemon juice, and Parmesan. Serve hot.

title: Garlic Mushrooms
notes: Serves 4. Prep 5 minutes, cook 10 minutes. Use a good quality dry white wine such as Pinot Gris, Chardonnay or Sauvignon Blanc. Wipe mushrooms clean with a damp cloth rather than rinsing, and don't crowd the pan if you want crisp edges. Leftovers keep in an airtight container in the fridge up to 3 days.
steps: Heat the butter and oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Sauté the onion until softened (about 3 minutes).
Add the mushrooms and cook for about 4-5 minutes until golden and crispy on the edges.
Pour in the wine and cook for 2 minutes, to reduce slightly.
Stir through thyme, 1 tablespoon of parsley and garlic. Cook for a further 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Season generously with salt and pepper (to your taste).
Sprinkle with remaining parsley and serve warm.

title: Spicy Avocado Salad
notes: Makes 3 servings. Prep 10 minutes. The hot sauce can be left out if you don't want the kick; a vinegar-and-cayenne style sauce is what the recipe intends. Cilantro can be swapped for dill or cherry tomatoes, and lemon juice works in place of lime.
steps: Place the chopped avocados, onion, bell pepper, and cilantro in a salad dish.
Top with the lime juice, olive oil, and hot sauce. Toss the salad so the vegetables are evenly coated.
Chill and serve.

title: Pickled Carrots
notes: Makes 8 servings of about 2 pieces each. Prep 1 hour 10 minutes, cook 10 minutes. The carrots aren't cooked — they soften slightly in the warm brine. Keeps 2-3 weeks in the fridge; not freezer friendly.
ingredients: ~1 lb carrots, tops removed, peeled if needed, sliced into sticks
2/3 cup distilled white or apple cider vinegar
1 Tbsp organic cane sugar (or stevia to taste)
steps: Add carrots to a large mason jar or glass container. Set aside.

To a small saucepan add distilled white vinegar, water, salt, and sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium heat and stir to fully dissolve salt and sugar. Taste and adjust flavor as needed, adding more salt or sugar to taste.
Pour the brine over the carrots, ensuring they are fully submerged. If needed, add more vinegar or a little water to cover.
Seal well and shake to combine. Then refrigerate for at least 1 hour. The flavors will deepen and intensify the longer it marinates. Best flavor is achieved after 24 hours.
Will keep in the refrigerator for 2-3 weeks (sometimes longer). Not freezer friendly.

title: Creamy Avocado-Basil Pasta with Corn and Tomatoes
notes: Serves 4. Prep 5 min, cook 20 min, cooling 5 min, total 30 min. Special equipment: large pot, colander, blender. Sour cream is thicker than crema and may need extra pasta water to loosen. Good warm or chilled as a pasta salad, but eat within 8 hours before the avocado sauce browns. Do not reheat - the sauce separates. Leftovers keep 4 days refrigerated, though the colour and freshness fade.
ingredients: 1 pound (450 g) short pasta such as fusilli or casarecce
4 medium ripe Hass avocados (about 23 ounces; 652 g), pitted, peeled, and chopped
2/3 cup (160 ml) crema or sour cream
6 tablespoons (90 ml) fresh lime juice (from 3 to 4 limes), plus finely grated lime zest for serving
1/2 cup (15 g) packed basil leaves, plus torn leaves for serving
1/3 cup (35 g) finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
3 teaspoons (9 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt, plus more to taste; for table salt use half as much by volume or the same weight
1 serrano chile (about 25 g), stemmed, seeded, and chopped
3/4 pound (340 g) cherry tomatoes, halved (about 2 cups)
1 1/2 cups cooked fresh or frozen corn kernels (7 1/2 ounces; 213 g)
8 ounces (227 g) canned or jarred hearts of palm, sliced into 1/4-inch coins (about 1 1/2 cups), optional
1/4 cup finely minced red onion, from 1 small onion (1 1/4 ounces; 35 g)
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pasta until al dente according to the package's instructions. Reserve 1 cup pasta water, then drain. Allow pasta to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a blender, combine avocados, crema, lime juice, basil, Parmesan, 3 teaspoons salt, serrano, garlic, and 1/4 cup reserved pasta water. Blend until smooth, adding 2 tablespoons of pasta water at a time as needed to achieve a smooth, creamy consistency, about 1 minute.

Transfer warm pasta to the now-empty pot or a large bowl. Add avocado sauce and toss well until pasta is evenly coated, adding additional pasta water 2 tablespoons at a time as needed until the sauce is creamy, glossy, and generously coats the pasta.
Fold in tomatoes, corn, hearts of palm, if using, and red onion. Taste and adjust with additional salt as needed.
Transfer to a serving bowl. Top with basil and lime zest. Serve.

title: Bean and sweet potato salad
notes: 3 servings. Prep 15 minutes, cook 15 minutes, total 30 minutes.
ingredients: 15 oz black beans, drained and rinsed
1 whole sweet potato, cut into cubes
steps: Pan fry sweet potato in olive oil and set aside to cool.
Drain and rinse kidney beans, black beans, and corn and add to a large bowl.
Add garlic salt, cilantro, and cooled sweet potato to the bowl of beans and stir.
Enjoy as is or use as a side dish.

title: roasted butternut squash
notes: Yields 6 to 8 servings. Prep 15 minutes, cook 55 minutes, total 1 hour 10 minutes.
ingredients: 2 medium butternut squash (4 to 5 pounds total)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.

Cut off and discard the ends of each butternut squash. Peel the squash, cut them in half lengthwise, and remove the seeds. Cut the squash into 1 1/4 to 1 1/2-inch cubes and place them on a baking sheet. Add the melted butter, brown sugar, salt, and pepper. With clean hands, toss all the ingredients together and spread in a single layer on the baking sheet. Roast for 45 to 55 minutes, until the squash is tender and the glaze begins to caramelize. While roasting, turn the squash a few times with a spatula, to be sure it browns evenly. Taste for seasonings and serve hot.

title: Keto Muschroom Wild Rice Pilaf
notes: Makes 4 servings of about 1/3 cup each. Prep 5 minutes, cook 15 minutes. There is no rice — shelled hemp hearts stand in for wild rice. Hemp seeds are very high in fat, so watch portion size. Pairs well with chicken, pork or beef.
steps: Wash and slice the mushrooms into small chunks.
Add butter to a pan over medium heat and let it melt and bubble. Once bubbling, add the slivered almonds and mushrooms to the pan.
Once the mushrooms are soft, add the hemp seeds to the pan. Mix together well.

Add the chicken broth and seasonings to the pan and stir together well. Turn the heat down to medium-low and let the chicken broth simmer and absorb into the mixture. Let cook until desired consistency is reached.
Serve and enjoy.

title: Black Beans
notes: Serves 12. Prep 10 minutes, cook about 1 hour 20 minutes. The beans are not soaked, which helps them hold their shape and makes a richer cooking liquid. Store in an airtight container in the fridge up to 5 days or freeze for several months, either drained or in their liquid. Kombu is optional and aids digestibility — keep it at a gentle simmer, as boiling turns it bitter.
ingredients: 8 cups water, plus more as needed
steps: Place the beans in a large colander and sort through them to remove and discard any stones or debris.

Rinse the beans and transfer them to a large pot or Dutch oven. Add the water, cumin, olive oil, salt, and several grinds of pepper and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat, add the kombu, if using, and simmer, uncovered, until the beans are tender. Check starting at 1 hour, and every 15 minutes after that. Depending on the freshness of your beans, it could take up to 2 1/2 hours. Add more water to the pot, as needed, to keep the beans submerged.
Remove the kombu and add the garlic during the last few minutes of cooking.

Season the beans as you like, adding chili powder, oregano, and more salt and pepper, if desired. Let the beans cool in the cooking liquid. Just before serving, stir in lime juice, zest, and cilantro, if desired.

title: Mexican Pasta Salad
notes: Yields 16 servings. Prep 10 minutes, cook 8 minutes. The sauce will be extremely runny right after you make it, but will thicken and adhere to the pasta as it chills in the fridge. Use gluten free pasta to make it gluten free. Keeps 5 days refrigerated.
ingredients: 1 (16 oz) box rotini pasta, cooked al dente according to package directions
1 (15 oz) can black beans, rinsed and drained
steps: Combine sauce ingredients in a food processor and blend until smooth. Taste and re-season as necessary.
Combine cooked (and drained) pasta, black beans, corn, and bell peppers in a large bowl.
Toss with sauce, cover (or place in large tupperware), and chill in the fridge for at least two hours, or overnight.
Serve cold!

title: Pasta Salad with Lemon-Pesto Dressing
notes: Yields 6 to 8 servings. Total 20 minutes: prep 10 minutes, cook 10 minutes.
ingredients: 1 pound cavatappi, corkscrew pasta, or medium shells
1 cup prepared pesto sauce from refrigerated case in supermarket
3/4 pound ricotta salata, chopped and crumbled, in specialty cheese case of market or 1 pound tub bocconcini mini pieces of mozzarella, drained, pieces halved
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it.
Place pesto, lemon zest, lemon juice, parsley, tomatoes, scallions and cheese in a large bowl.
Cook pasta to al dente then cold shock it and chill it down under cold running water. Drain well. Add to mixing bowl. Combine salad and season with salt and pepper, to taste.

title: Creamy Potato and Prosciutto Salad
notes: Yields 4 to 6 servings. Total 35 minutes plus at least 1 hour refrigeration: prep 5 minutes, cook 30 minutes.
ingredients: 2 pounds baby tricolor or red bliss potatoes, quartered
Kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
steps: Make the salad: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Brush a baking sheet with the olive oil and arrange the prosciutto in a single layer. Bake until the fat is rendered and the prosciutto is crisp, 12 to 14 minutes. Remove the prosciutto to a rack and let cool completely, then break into pieces and set aside.

Meanwhile, fill a large pot with cold water; add the potatoes and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium low and simmer until the potatoes are just fork-tender, about 15 minutes. (The potatoes will continue to cook when you remove them from the water, and you don't want a mushy potato salad!) Drain in a colander, then place the colander over the now-empty pot, off the heat, to allow the excess moisture to evaporate from the potatoes.
Make the dressing: In a large bowl, whisk the mayonnaise, scallions, sugar, paprika, mustard and vinegar. Taste and then season with salt and a few grinds of pepper.
Add the potatoes to the bowl with the dressing and gently toss. Refrigerate at least 1 hour. Sprinkle the crispy prosciutto on top before serving.

title: Garlic and Herb Grilled Sweet Potato Fries
notes: Yields 6 servings. Total 35 minutes: prep 10 minutes, cook 25 minutes.
ingredients: 2 teaspoons finely chopped fresh thyme leaves
2 tablespoons finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley
steps: Place the potatoes in a large pot of cold water, add 2 tablespoons of salt and cook until potatoes are tender, but still firm, about 15 minutes. Drain and let cool slightly.
Heat the grill to high.

While the potatoes are cooling, heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a small saute pan on the grates of the grill. Add the garlic, thyme and chili flakes and cook until the garlic is just soft, about 45 seconds. Remove from the heat.

Slice each potato in half lengthwise then slice each half into 3 or 4 wedges, depending on the size. Brush the wedges with the remaining 3 tablespoons of oil and season with salt. Grill until lightly golden brown and just cooked through, about 6 minutes. Remove to a platter and immediately toss with the garlic mixture and chopped parsley.

title: Mediterranean Tuna Pasta
notes: Yields 4 servings. Prep 20 minutes, cook 15 minutes. If using good quality tuna packed in high quality olive oil there is no need to drain it. If you can't find fusilli, substitute another pasta with nooks and crannies like rotini, campanelle, conchiglie, or farfalle. Keeps 5 to 6 days in the fridge; warm in the microwave 30 to 60 seconds before serving.
ingredients: 2 (5-ounce) cans of albacore tuna (preferably packed in olive oil), drained
1 tomato, cored, cut in half crosswise and squeezed of excess juice, chopped (about 1 cup)
1/4 cup kalamata olives, pitted and coarsely chopped
2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil (more if you are using tuna packed in water)
steps: Put the pasta water on to boil: Heat 2 quarts of salted water (1 tablespoon kosher salt) to a boil. While heating the pasta water, prep the ingredients.

Place drained tuna in a medium bowl. Stir with a fork to break up the largest chunks of tuna. Add the tomato, olives, red onion, parsley, capers, lemon juice, olive oil (if needed), salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.

When the water comes to a boil, add the pasta and bring back to a boil. Cook, uncovered, at a rolling boil until al dente (cooked through, but still a little firm to the bite), about 6 to 9 minutes more. Reserve 1/4 cup of the pasta water.

Drain the pasta and immediately add the hot pasta to the tuna mixture. Sprinkle with the grated mozzarella cheese and stir until everything is well combined. If the pasta seems a little dry, add some of the reserved pasta water and/or some more olive oil.
Serve warm as a light lunch or a dinner side.

title: Lemon Mushroom Orzo
notes: Yields 12 servings. Prep 15 minutes, cook 10 minutes. Can be served chilled or hot.
steps: Cook orzo according to package directions. Meanwhile, in a large cast-iron or other heavy skillet, heat 2 tablespoons oil over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms; cook and stir until tender and lightly browned. Drain orzo.
In a large bowl, place orzo, mushroom mixture, pecans, parsley, lemon zest, lemon juice, salt, pepper and remaining 1 tablespoon oil; toss to combine.

title: Bruschetta Pasta Salad
notes: Yields 4 servings. Prep 15 minutes, total 25 minutes. Any small pasta shape works - farfalle, penne, or fusilli. For a cheesy version add freshly grated Parmesan or mozzarella pearls. Letting it rest in the fridge up to an hour develops the flavors. Leftovers keep about 4 days in an airtight container.
ingredients: 1 pt. cherry tomatoes, preferably multi-colored, halved
steps: In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook orecchiette according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil and balsamic vinegar, then season with salt and pepper.
To bowl, add pasta, garlic and tomatoes; toss with dressing to combine.
Garnish with basil and serve.

title: Strawberry Balsamic Salad
notes: Yields 6 to 8 servings. Prep 20 minutes, total 40 minutes. To make balsamic glaze at home, simmer 1 cup balsamic vinegar in a small saucepan over medium heat until thickened and reduced by about half.
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh basil leaves, torn if large
1/2 cup fresh mint leaves, torn if large
Store-bought or homemade balsamic glaze, for drizzling
steps: In a large pot of boiling salted water, cook pasta, stirring occasionally, until al dente according to package directions. Drain and rinse under cold water. Drain again.

Meanwhile, in a small skillet over medium heat, heat 1/4 cup oil. Add almonds and cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant and lightly golden, 2 to 3 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer almonds to a paper towel-lined plate. Reserve oil in skillet; season with salt. Transfer oil to a large bowl and whisk in vinegar, syrup, mustard, and remaining 1/4 cup oil; season with salt and pepper.

To bowl with vinegar mixture, add pasta, strawberries, shallots, spinach, basil, and mint. Toss to coat; season with salt and pepper, if needed. Add almonds and cheese and gently toss to combine. Drizzle with balsamic glaze.

title: Mediterranean Orzo Salad
notes: Yields 6 servings. Prep 15 minutes, cook 11 minutes. Good warm or cold. The dressing can be made up to 5 days ahead of time.
ingredients: 6 oz dry gluten free orzo pasta
1 cup grape or cherry tomatoes, sliced in half
1 clove garlic, microplaned or finely minced
steps: Cook orzo according to package directions then drain and set aside to cool slightly.

For the Lemon Dressing: Combine olive oil, lemon juice, honey, garlic, salt, and pepper in a mason jar with a tight fitting lid then shake to combine. Alternatively, add lemon juice, salt, pepper, honey and garlic to a food processor then process while slowly drizzling in olive oil.

Add slightly cooled pasta to a large mixing bowl with tomatoes, olives, feta cheese, parsley, and capers. Drizzle on enough Lemon Dressing to coat then toss to combine. Chill for 10-15 minutes before serving then add additional dressing if desired.

title: Mediterranean Quinoa Salad
notes: Amounts were not captured from the page - check the source for measurements. Yields 4 servings. Prep 10 minutes, cook 15 minutes. Make ahead by keeping the dressing separate and dressing only right before serving; no more than a day in advance so the basil stays fresh. Keeps 2 days dressed, up to 4 days undressed. Does not freeze well.
ingredients: Quinoa (white quinoa recommended), cooked and cooled
Olive oil (for the lemon oregano dressing)
Fresh lemon juice (for the lemon oregano dressing)
Dried oregano (for the lemon oregano dressing)
steps: Cook the quinoa according to package directions and let it cool completely.
Chop up all the veggies into small pieces.
To prepare the salad mix all the ingredients together in a large bowl. If there is any ingredient you like more of feel free to add more.
Mix all the salad dressing ingredients together in a small jar. Cover with the lid and shake until incorporated.
Pour half the salad dressing onto the quinoa salad and give it a taste. If you like more dressing, add more. Otherwise reserve leftover dressing for other salads.

title: Garlic Parmesan Brussels Sprouts
notes: Yields 4 servings. Prep 10 minutes, cook 40 minutes, total 50 minutes.
steps: Remove the stem from each sprout and cut in half. Place the brussels sprouts in a large bowl.
Add the rest of the ingredients to the bowl and toss to cover.
Spread the sprouts onto a baking sheet.
Bake in a 400˚F (200˚C) oven for 20 minutes.
Flip the sprouts, then bake for an additional 20 minutes or until the sprouts are fork-tender and golden.

title: Garlic Tumeric Parsnip Fries
notes: Yields 4 servings. Prep 5 minutes, cook 30 minutes. Nutritional yeast substitutes for the parmesan to make these dairy-free or vegan. Peeling is optional - young, small parsnips don't need it. They may lose crispness when reheated; reheat under the broiler to crisp them back up.
ingredients: 1/4 cup avocado oil or olive oil
steps: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Slice parsnips in even slices and toss in small bowl with avocado oil. Add garlic and turmeric.
Transfer parsnips to baking sheet. Sprinkle with sea salt and parmesan cheese and bake for 15 minutes.
Take baking sheet out and carefully flip parsnips with a spatula. Sprinkle with more parmesan cheese. Return to oven and bake for 15 more minutes, until parsnips are evenly browned.

title: Cinnamon Yams with Honey
notes: Yields 4 servings. Total 45 minutes: prep 15 minutes, cook 30 minutes. Cut the cubes to a similar size and arrange in a single layer without crowding - if they touch or overlap they steam instead of roast.
ingredients: 4 sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling potatoes after cooked
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Lay the sweet potatoes out in a single layer on a roasting tray. Drizzle the oil, honey, cinnamon, salt and pepper over the potatoes. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes in oven or until tender.
Take sweet potatoes out of the oven and transfer them to a serving platter. Drizzle with more extra-virgin olive oil.

title: Brussels Sprouts with Bread Crumbs
notes: Serves 10. Prep 15 minutes, cook 15 minutes, total 30 minutes.
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 1/3 pounds brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
steps: In a small skillet, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the panko bread crumbs and cook, stirring occasionally, until the bread crumbs are lightly golden brown, about 4 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from the heat.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the pancetta and cook until the fat renders and the pancetta is crisp, about 4 minutes. Transfer the pancetta with a slotted spoon to paper towels.
Add the brussels sprouts to the pan, season generously with salt and pepper, and sauté until tender, 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the lemon zest and juice to the pan and stir to combine. Transfer the brussels sprouts to a large serving bowl or platter and top with the bread crumbs and pancetta.

title: Mashed Sweet Potato
notes: Serves 8. Prep 10 minutes, cook 8 minutes. No steamer basket needed and no need to drain the cooking water — it keeps the potatoes moist. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container up to 4 days, or freeze flat in zip-top bags (leave out the seasonings). For vegan, use coconut butter or vegan butter; for paleo or Whole30, use coconut butter or ghee.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon dried thyme or your favorite seasoning
2 tablespoons butter, vegan butter, ghee, or coconut butter
steps: Peel and chop your sweet potatoes into approximately 1-inch chunks. Place the chunks into the base of a 6-quart or 8-quart pressure cooker.
Add the salt, thyme, and cinnamon to the sweet potatoes and toss to combine.
Pour in the water and lock the lid on the pressure cooker. Set the time to 8 minutes at high pressure.
When the cooking time is up, use the quick-release to release the pressure.
Carefully remove the lid and stir in the maple syrup and butter, vegan butter, ghee, or coconut butter to the potatoes.
Use a spatula or a potato masher to mix together and serve hot.

title: Greek Salad
notes: Makes 4 servings. Prep 15 minutes, no cooking. Best enjoyed within 2-3 days of making. For a crowd, double everything — the salad can be made 1-2 days ahead and the veggies marinate beautifully in the dressing. Add diced avocado for extra healthy fats, or a cup of cooked quinoa, grilled shrimp, salmon, or cubed chicken for more protein.
ingredients: 1 (15 ounce) can of chickpeas, rinsed and drained
15 grape tomatoes, halved (about 1 cup halved grape tomatoes)
1/3 cup pitted kalamata olives, chopped if desired
4 ounces feta cheese, crumbled or cut into 1/2 inch cubes
freshly ground salt and pepper, to taste
steps: Place all salad ingredients into a large bowl and toss to combine.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, garlic and oregano. Pour onto salad and toss again to well combine. Taste and add salt and pepper as you'd like.
Place in refrigerator for 1 hour to marinate, or serve immediately.

title: Yellow Rice
notes: Serves 4. Prep 10 minutes, cook 20 minutes. You can substitute saffron for the turmeric. All the ingredients can also go straight into a rice cooker. Variations: add frozen peas or carrots while cooking; go Cajun with diced onion, bell pepper and jalapeño sauteed with the rice; or Mexican-style with jalapeño, onion, and a sprinkle of cumin before adding the broth.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon onion powder, or dried minced onion
1/2 teaspoon Kosher salt, or to taste
steps: Heat butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the rice and gently stir until rice begins to lightly brown.
Add garlic, onion powder, and turmeric and stir until well mixed in.
Slowly stir in chicken broth and raise heat to medium-high. Add salt and pepper to taste. Bring the mix to a boil then turn the heat to low and cover the pan with a lid. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes.
Remove from heat, add cilantro, and fluff with a fork.

title: Fried Rice
notes: Takes about 15 minutes. Thoroughly chilled cooked rice is essential — warm rice turns soggy and clumpy in the pan. If cooking fresh, spread it on a sheet pan, cover, and chill 30 minutes in the fridge or 10-15 in the freezer. A nonstick or cast-iron pan works best. Sesame oil is a finishing oil, so add it off the heat.
ingredients: 4 cups cooked and chilled rice (short-grain white rice preferred)
3–4 tablespoons soy sauce, or more to taste
steps: Heat 1/2 tablespoon of butter in a large saute pan over medium-high heat until melted. Add egg, and cook until scrambled, stirring occasionally. Remove egg, and transfer to a separate plate.

Add an additional 1 tablespoon butter to the pan and heat until melted. Add carrots, onion, peas and garlic, and season with a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Saute for about 5 minutes or until the onion and carrots are soft.

Increase heat to high, add in the remaining 1 1/2 tablespoons of butter, and stir until melted. Immediately add the rice, green onions, soy sauce and oyster sauce (if using), and stir until combined. Continue sauteing for an additional 3 minutes to fry the rice, stirring occasionally — let the rice rest between stirs so it can crisp up on the bottom.
Add in the eggs and stir to combine. Remove from heat, and stir in the sesame oil until combined. Taste and season with extra soy sauce, if needed.
Serve immediately, or refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 3 days.

title: Zoodles
notes: 4 servings. Prep 8 minutes, cook 12 minutes. No spiralizer? Use a julienne peeler, mandoline, or standard vegetable peeler for wide ribbons. To avoid soggy zoodles, salt only at the end of cooking and use the cornstarch slurry. Best eaten immediately; leftovers keep a couple of days but release more liquid. For a vegetarian version, swap the parmesan for a vegetarian-friendly cheese or nutritional yeast.
ingredients: 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, depending on how spicy you like the pasta
1/2 cup shredded parmesan cheese, plus more for serving
1 cup basil leaves, torn into pieces
steps: Trim and spiralize the zucchini. Then cut the spiralized zucchini into long noodles to be about the length of spaghetti.
Add olive oil, garlic, and the red pepper flakes to a large, deep skillet. Turn to medium heat. When the oil bubbles around the garlic, add the zucchini noodles.

Toss the noodles with pasta tongs and cook until al dente — they should be wilted but still have a crunch; 5 to 7 minutes. Do not let the noodles cook any longer, or else they will become mushy. As they cook, keep tossing so that all the zucchini noodles have a chance to hit the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in the tomatoes, basil, and parmesan cheese, and then cook for one minute. Use pasta tongs to transfer the noodles, tomatoes, and basil to a serving dish. Leave the liquid in the skillet.
Bring the liquid left in the skillet to a simmer.

Combine cornstarch and cold water in a small bowl, then whisk into the simmering liquid. Cook while whisking until the liquid thickens to a sauce; about 1 minute. Taste the sauce and season with salt.
Pour the sauce over the zucchini, tomatoes, and basil. Finish with more parmesan cheese on top and serve immediately.

title: Crockpot Corn
notes: 8 servings. Prep 5 minutes, cook 2 hours 30 minutes. You can pack the slow cooker to capacity as long as the lid seals — it may just take a little longer. Frozen corn works too: add the water, pile in the corn, and cook 3.5-4.5 hours on high. Leftovers keep 3-4 days in the fridge or up to a month in the freezer.
steps: Remove the husks from corn. Add water to the slow cooker and then pile the corn in and cover.
Cook on high for 2.5-3.5 hours. Corn will be bright and tender when ready.
While cooking, combine all ingredients for the garlic butter together and mix well.
Once the corn is done, brush on all sides with the garlic butter. There will be enough butter for 8 large ears of corn.

title: Mexican Street Corn
notes: Serves 6. Prep 5 minutes, cook 8 minutes. Fresh corn can be used: brush husked cobs with vegetable oil, grill on high, turning every 2-3 minutes until slightly charred, then cut the kernels off. Substitutions: feta or parmesan for the cotija, parsley for the cilantro, Mexican crema or Greek yogurt for the mayo. Serve warm or cold. Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge up to 3 days.
steps: Heat a cast iron skillet on high heat and add the corn. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and add in butter and salt. Stir until mixed.
Place corn in a bowl and stir in mayo and lime juice. Add 1 teaspoon chili powder and mix well.
Sprinkle with cotija cheese, chili powder, and chopped cilantro. Serve immediately.

title: Chicken with Satay sauce
notes: 4 servings. You can also thread the chicken pieces on a skewer and grill them in the oven or on the barbecue. Use coconut cream containing about 35% fat.
steps: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and place in a bowl or a plastic bag.
Add the ginger, garlic, turmeric, lime, and tamari. Let marinate for 10 minutes.
While the chicken is marinating, combine the ingredients for the satay sauce in a small saucepan and bring to a boil.
Let simmer on low heat for 5-10 minutes until the sauce is of desired consistency. Season to taste and keep warm.
Heat a wok or large frying pan on medium-high heat with coconut oil. Add the garlic and fry the chicken and broccoli until the chicken is thoroughly cooked.
Serve the sauce with the chicken and broccoli. Sprinkle with crushed peanuts and fresh cilantro for extra crunch and flavor.

title: Pad Thai
notes: Serves 4. Prep 15 minutes, cook 15 minutes. Substitute 2 tablespoons tamarind paste for the rice vinegar for a more authentic sauce. Make ahead by cutting the protein, chopping the veggies, and stirring the sauce together in advance. For vegan or vegetarian, leave out the egg, use tofu, and swap the fish sauce for more soy sauce. Leftovers keep 2-3 days in the fridge.
ingredients: 8 ounces uncooked shrimp, chicken, or extra-firm tofu, cut into small pieces
2 Tablespoons rice vinegar, or tamarind paste
1 Tablespoon Sriracha hot sauce, or more, to taste
steps: Cook noodles according to package instructions, just until tender. Rinse under cold water.
Make sauce by combining sauce ingredients in a bowl. Set aside.

Heat 1 1/2 tablespoons of oil in a wok or large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the shrimp, chicken or tofu, garlic and bell pepper. The shrimp will cook quickly, about 1-2 minutes on each side, or until pink. If using chicken, cook until just cooked through, about 3-4 minutes, flipping only once.
Push everything to the side of the pan. Add a little more oil and add the beaten eggs. Scramble the eggs, breaking them into small pieces with a spatula as they cook.
Add noodles, sauce, bean sprouts and peanuts to the wok (reserving some peanuts for topping at the end). Toss everything to combine.
Garnish the top with green onions, extra peanuts, cilantro and lime wedges. Serve immediately.

title: Fiesta Salmon
notes: 4 servings. Prep 20 minutes, cook 40 minutes. Good for meal prep — store in airtight containers in the fridge for 3-5 days, but wait to add the sliced avocado and yogurt until just before serving. The page links out to a separate cilantro lime rice tutorial; the step above is assembled from the listed ingredients.
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon salt, or more to taste
1 cup uncooked long-grain white rice, or long-grain brown rice
1/4 teaspoon sea salt, or more, to taste
15 oz. can corn, drained and rinsed (or 1 1/2 cups frozen corn)
15 oz. can black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: First, prepare the salmon by patting the filets dry with a piece of paper towel.

Next, bake, pan fry, or grill your salmon. In the oven: bake at 375ºF for 20-25 minutes or until it's light pink in color and easy to flake. On the grill: grill at 450ºF skin-side down for about 6 minutes, then flip and grill for 2 more minutes or until the salmon reaches 140ºF internally. On the stovetop: pan-sear over medium/high heat for 4 minutes skin-side up, then flip and cook for 3-4 more minutes or until light pink and flakey.
Prepare the cilantro lime rice by cooking the rice in the water, then stirring in the cilantro, lime juice, garlic powder, and sea salt.
Next, add corn, black beans, and red onion to a medium-sized bowl and mix well.
Evenly distribute around 1/2 cup of the corn mixture into each bowl (you will have leftovers).
Place a serving of cooked salmon into each bowl. Then, slice 2 large avocados and add half an avocado to each bowl.
Make the dressing by whisking the olive oil, chopped cilantro, lime juice, and salt together in a bowl and drizzle over each bowl.
Finally, serve with Greek yogurt/sour cream and your favorite chips.

title: Lemon Chicken
notes: 4 servings. Prep 18 minutes, cook 12 minutes. To prep ahead, slice the chicken and let it sit in the egg mixture in the fridge — it makes the chicken juicier. Works with chicken breast, thighs, or tenderloins; adjust cook time to reach 165˚F. Reduce the lemon juice if you prefer a less tangy sauce. Asparagus, green beans, or zucchini can be added to the skillet.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb chicken breast (2 large), patted dry with paper towels
steps: Cut the chicken breasts in half lengthwise. Lightly beat with a meat mallet until even in thickness.

In a bowl, whisk together the ingredients for the egg mixture. In another bowl, combine the ingredients for the parmesan mixture. Dip chicken into the egg mixture, then dredge chicken in the parmesan mixture. Allow any excess ingredients to fall off from each bowl.

In a large non-stick skillet, heat enough oil to cover the bottom of a skillet. Once hot, add the chicken and cook 4-5 minutes per side, or until crispy, golden and cooked through to 165˚F on an Instant Read Thermometer. Reduce the heat if chicken browns too quickly.

Meanwhile, in a separate saucepan, melt butter and garlic, cook until fragrant. Add the chicken broth, lemon juice and pepper. Allow the sauce to cook for about 2 minutes. Pour the sauce over the cooked chicken, turning to coat. Garnish with lemon slices and finely chopped parsley if desired.

title: Caprese Chicken Thighs
notes: 6 servings. Prep 10 minutes, cook 45 minutes. Thighs stay tender where breasts would dry out. Quite a bit of the olive oil is left in the bottom of the pan after baking — use it for a side dish if you like. Good with zucchini ribbons or a side salad.
steps: Preheat your oven to 350°F. Preheat a cast iron (or other oven-safe) skillet over medium-high heat. Add the butter and allow it to melt.
Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper then lay them down in the skillet.
Let the chicken thighs brown for several minutes until they are golden, before flipping over and cooking the other side.
In a food processor blend the basil leaves, olive oil, and pine nuts. Season with additional salt.
Turn off the heat under the skillet. Spoon the pesto sauce over the chicken thighs.
Layer with the tomato and mozzarella.
Bake for about 30 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked all the way through and the cheese is melted and browned.

title: Enchilada Skillet Chicken
notes: 4 servings. Prep 10 minutes, cook 30 minutes. Canned enchilada sauce keeps it simple, but homemade works and green enchilada sauce is a good swap. Serve with zucchini noodles or a side salad.
steps: Split the chicken breasts, horizontally, into two even pieces. Preheat your skillet over medium-high heat and add butter. Turn your oven on to 400°F.
Season both sides of the chicken with salt and pepper.
Press into the almond flour and evenly coat both sides.
Whisk the eggs together, then dip the chicken into the egg and coat both sides.

Lay the chicken down into the pan and brown on both sides. Do two at a time and place the finished pieces on a plate while you cook the next batch. Don't worry about cooking the chicken through, just brown the coating.
If some of the egg has gotten stuck on the pan you will want to deglaze it with some water and wipe it out. When all the pieces are browned, return the chicken to the skillet.
Pour the red enchilada sauce over the top of the chicken pieces.
Sprinkle on the diced onion and shredded cheese.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, until hot and bubbly.

title: Dijon Pork Loin
notes: 6 servings. Prep 10 minutes, cook 40 minutes. Pork is done at 63°C | 145°F. No marinating needed — the sear and sauce carry the flavor. Keep the potatoes crisp by patting them very dry, preheating the pan, and not crowding or over-stirring. If you don't own an oven-safe skillet, transfer the pork and potatoes to a baking dish for the roast.
ingredients: 1 pound baby potatoes, quartered and patted dry with paper towels
1 tablespoon Dijon mustard, mild and smooth
1 pound green beans, trimmed and halved
2 tablespoons fresh rosemary, chopped, or thyme
steps: Preheat oven to 220°C | 440°F. Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large skillet (12-14 inch) or pan over medium-high heat. When skillet is hot, add in the potatoes. Sprinkle with salt and pepper, and fry for 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until crisp on the edges.
While potatoes are cooking, pat pork dry with paper towel and season with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, whisk together honey, mustards, garlic and 1 tablespoon oil. Pour two thirds of the sauce over the tenderloins to coat evenly, and reserve the remaining sauce for cooking later.
Push the potatoes to one side of the skillet and add in the tenderloins, searing them for a couple of minutes on all sides (use tongs to turn them so they slightly brown on all four sides).
Baste the pork with the remaining sauce, sprinkle with the fresh herbs and transfer skillet to the hot oven. (If you don't have a skillet, transfer pork and potatoes to a large baking dish.)

Roast for about 15 minutes, or until potatoes are 'just' fork tender. Remove skillet (or dish) from oven, add the green beans to the skillet/dish around the tenderloins and potatoes; and transfer back into the oven. Continue cooking until the pork is cooked to your liking and the green beans are tender (about 6-10 minutes, depending on your oven).
Once the tenderloins are cooked, let rest for 5 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Parmegan Crusted Pork Chops
notes: Serves 4. Prep 6 minutes, cook 12 minutes. Cooking time varies with chop thickness (these were ¾ - 1 inch); increase or decrease accordingly and check with an instant read thermometer - 145F for medium, 160F for well - then rest 10-15 minutes before cutting. If you don't have pork rinds you can use almond flour instead, but watch for burning. The crust mixture is just enough for 4 chops; the recipe halves nicely but try 4-5 minutes per side.
ingredients: 1 ¼ pound boneless pork chops (4 chops)
2 tablespoon avocado oil or olive oil
½ cup grated Parmesan cheese, (2 oz)
steps: Let the pork come to room temperature for 20-30 minutes before beginning. Pat the pork dry with a paper towel. Season well with salt and pepper. Beat the egg and water in a shallow bowl large enough to fit a pork chop.

Place the grated Parmesan cheese and crushed pork rinds onto a large dinner plate. Mince the garlic and parsley and add to the cheese. Zest a small lemon, adding the zest to the plate. Mix well with fingers to combine ingredients.

Heat a large frying pan over medium heat until hot. Using a fork, place a pork chop into the egg mixture, flipping it over a few times to fully coat. Let any extra egg run off before placing the pork chop into the Parmesan coating. Push and wiggle it into the mixture, making sure it is completely coated.
Pour the oil into the pan and swirl to coat. Add the crumbed pork chop and put it into the pan. Repeat the breading procedure with the remaining pork chops.

When the pork chops are all in the pan, set the timer for 3 minutes. When time is up flip the 1st pork chop. Wait 1 minute and flip the next. Wait another minute and flip the third pork chop. Wait 1 minute and flip the last pork chop.

Set the timer again for 3 minutes. Check the pork by pressing the top lightly with the finger. If it's squishy, it's not done. If it's firm, it's done. Pork should be cooked until the internal temperature is 140 F. (Carry-over cooking will take it to 145 F as it rests.) Use an instant read thermometer to check.

When time is up, remove the 1st chop to a plate and tent loosely with foil. Remove the remaining pork chops to the plate 1 minute apart just like you did for flipping. Let rest for 10 minutes and serve.

title: Keto Chicken Peanut Pad Thai
notes: Serves 4. Prep 15 minutes, cook 15 minutes. Needs a spiralizer for the zucchini noodles.
steps: In a wok or a large pan on medium heat, cook the chopped onion in olive oil until translucent. Then cook the garlic until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Season the boneless skinless chicken thighs with salt and pepper and place them in the wok. Let them cook for about 5-7 minutes on each side or until fully cooked.
Take the chicken thighs out of the wok and shred them using two forks.
Trim the ends off the zucchini and spiralize them into thin noodles. Set the noodles aside.
Create a well in the center of the wok or pan and crack an egg into it. Allow it to cook for a few seconds and then scramble it into large chunks.
Once the egg is cooked, toss the zucchini noodles into the pan. Let your noodles cook for just about 2 minutes, tossing continuously.
Add the shredded chicken thighs and finish it all off with a splash of soy sauce, lime juice and chili flakes, if using.
Serve the Chicken Pad Thai with crushed or whole peanuts and lime for garnish. Salt and pepper the dish as needed.

title: Slow Cooker Pork Tenderloin
notes: Serves 6. Prep 15 minutes, cook 8 hours. The sauce recipe makes enough to drizzle over the pork when serving; double it for extra saucy pork. The sauce can be made with other fruits or berries (raspberries, orange, pomegranate). Shredded pork keeps well in the fridge for hash, salads, burrito bowls, tacos, sandwiches and soups, and freezes well.
steps: Salt and pepper pork tenderloin. Sear pork in large pan over high heat.
Oil the bottom of a 6qt slow cooker. Transfer pork tenderloin to slow cooker. Add stock and sage.
Cook on low for 8-9 hours. (Cooking on high is not recommended as it can cause the pork to dry out.)
Remove pork from slow cooker and shred. It should be falling apart.
Pulse blackberries in blender. Push blackberry mixture through mesh strainer. Discard seeds.
In a 3.5qt pot, bring blackberry pulp, vinegar, olive oil and salt to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer 15-20 minutes while whisking occasionally. Vigorously whisk the last 2-3 minutes.
Once the sauce reaches a syrupy consistency, set aside to cool and thicken for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Slow Cooker Pork Carnitas
notes: Serves 6-8. Prep 10 minutes, cook 8 hours. Use pork shoulder or pork butt - the higher fat content gives the most tender result, and bone-in or boneless both work. Save the drippings for reheating to keep the pork juicy. Refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to 3 months. Can be made with chicken breasts or thighs instead: cook 4-5 hours on low, then broil as directed.
ingredients: 1 4-5 pound pork shoulder/pork butt, trimmed of excess fat
steps: Heat oil in a large pan over high heat. Add the pork and sear on each side until browned, about 1-2 minutes per side. Transfer pork to a large slow cooker.
Add the remaining ingredients to the slow cooker. Cook on low for 8 hours or on high for 4-5 hours or until the pork is tender. Remove the bay leaves.
Remove the meat from the slow cooker and shred. (Make sure to keep the liquid.)
Transfer the shredded pork to a baking sheet and broil for 5 minutes or until crispy.
Remove from the oven and pour 1/4 cup of the reserved juices from the slow cooker onto the crispy pork and toss.

Place the baking sheet back in the broiler for an additional 5 minutes or until the meat is crispy. Pour an additional 1/4 cup liquid over the crispy pork and serve immediately with cilantro, if desired.

title: Slow Cooker Mushroom Pot Roast
notes: Yield 8 servings. Prep 15 minutes, cook 4 hours. The mushroom bouillon cubes or concentrate are what make the pot roast so flavorful - check the label if you need it gluten-free or Paleo. Regular white mushrooms work in place of Cremini. A 6-quart slow cooker was used, but any size that holds the roast and mushrooms will work.
ingredients: 2 mushroom stock cubes or 2 T mushroom stock base + 1/2 cup water
3 1/2 lb. chuck roast (before trimming), fat trimmed (cut apart as needed to cut out the fat)
2 T steak rub for rubbing the meat before browning (more or less to taste)
1 tsp. onion powder for rubbing the meat before browning
3/4 tsp. kosher salt for rubbing the meat before browning (use less if your steak rub has salt)
1/2 tsp. fresh ground pepper for rubbing the meat before browning
1 1/2 lbs. Cremini mushrooms (or less, to taste)
steps: Put the mushroom cubes or stock base into a glass measuring cup with 1/2 cup of water and microwave until the mushroom base has dissolved into the water, about a minute. Stir to combine.
Trim the roast, removing most of the fat even if you have to cut the roast into sections to get the fat off.
Mix the steak rub, onion powder, salt, and black pepper. Rub all sides of the meat generously with the spice mixture.

Heat the oil in a non-stick or cast-iron frying pan and brown the meat well on all sides. This will take about 5-7 minutes; don't rush the browning step. When the meat is nicely browned, put it into the slow cooker.

Pour the mushroom stock mixture into the frying pan and cook on high for 1-2 minutes, scraping with the turner to remove any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Pour the liquid over the meat in the slow cooker.
Cook on HIGH for 3 hours.

Wash mushrooms and cut into thick slices. Put mushrooms over the meat in the slow cooker and cook 45-60 minutes more, or until mushrooms are cooked and the meat feels tender when you pierce it with a fork.
Scoop out the meat and mushrooms with a slotted spoon; put the mushrooms in a bowl and the meat on a cutting board.
Strain the juice and taste to see if you want to simmer it to reduce and intensify the flavor.
Slice the meat, arrange on a platter, and serve with mushrooms and mushroom au jus.
If you don't care about low-carb you can thicken the au jus with some cornstarch and make gravy.

title: Slow Cooker Honey Garlic Chicken
notes: Serves 4-6. Prep 10 minutes, cook 2 hours (HIGH) or 5-6 hours (LOW). Use skinless, bone-in chicken thighs; skin-on thighs are fine as long as you sear the skin to render some fat so it doesn't melt into the sauce. If you prefer it less sweet, add a splash of rice vinegar or a squeeze of lemon juice at the end.
ingredients: 6 large chicken thighs, skinless and bone-in
6 cloves garlic, finely chopped or minced
2 tablespoons rice wine vinegar or cider vinegar
steps: Pat dry bone-in, skinless chicken thighs with paper towel. Combine 1/2 tablespoon of oil with rub ingredients. Season chicken, rubbing the mixture into the chicken.

OPTIONAL SEAR: Heat remaining 1/2 tablespoon oil in a large pan or skillet over medium heat. Sear chicken for 2 minutes each side to get a nice sear. (Do not cook chicken all the way through, this step is purely for flavour.)
Transfer chicken thighs to a 6-qt (litre) slow cooker bowl.
